summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (104/38)

data.turoyo: W maltamle zlame, d kətwayne rešone w d kətwayne ann abne dam malke w d kətwayne ann abne daš šyux w maḥtile ʕal aw waḏ̣ayəf w mratable i dawlayḏe.
data.translation: Dann suchte er edle, vornehme Männer zusammen, Söhne von Königen, Söhne von Scheichen, setzte sie in die Beamtenstellen ein und ordnete sein reich aufs Neue.

rationale: First Preterit box; explicit state object and appointment context exemplify arranging an institution.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Jan 1.41/1826)

data.turoyo: <...> Šexo Slaymano kəmmi, ḥa mas sayome du šuġlo yo. Ḥa ma mratbone du šuġlo yo. <...>
data.translation: <...> Shekho Slaymono, they say, was one of those who did the deed, one of those who organized the deed. <...>

rationale: New Part act. box, provisionally indexing the attested plural organiser noun; hearsay attribution retained.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.18/3707)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d kmaḥkenolox d Aġa Bəṭrəs w du Ingiliz w d Rusya w fəlan d mwaʕədalle d saymile dukṯo b iḏe d mtartəbile, d mratbile.
data.translation: The time I am telling you about Agha Petros and the English and Russia and so on, who had promised him that they would put a place in his hands, that they would arrange it for him, that they would organize it for him.

rationale: First Infectum example; exact adjacent mtartəbile/mratbile sequence preserved, without making the uncertain first shape a new rtb form.

summary: 26/202 is already the sole Imperativ quotation; the reader's thin-cell add request would duplicate it.
104/38 supplies the inherited base mratable as an actual Preterit attestation, not a new stem. Its state object is zero-marked.
Reflexive ruḥayxu at26/202 uses active II morphology. The institutional object at104/38 is ordinary verbal valency, not sufficient reason for a light verb idiom.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
Round one already supplies Preterit; Jan adds secure Infectum and a provisional Part act. organiser formation. No sense renumbering or repeated round-one proposal is needed.
du šuġlo depends on the organiser noun at 1826. It is not evidence of a light verb plus noun idiom, nor proof that the noun is a freely productive participle.
The extra-t mtartəbile is immediately followed by mratbile. The exact source is retained, but analogy with an Arabic noun cannot independently establish its root or stem.
The -le in the plural Infectum context is a recipient/beneficiary index; dukṯo is the understood arranged entity. A promise context does not require Infectum-wa merely because English uses would.

Does institutional rtb specifically imply reorganization of something already established? The edition says aufs Neue, but the Turoyo has no separate again expression; the entry should not encode that implication from German alone.
Is mratbone a productive Part act. or a lexical organiser noun? The Part act. indexing remains provisional.
Does mtartəbile at 3707 reflect a repair, a trtb loan formation, or an rtb variant? Do not regularise it without source/speaker confirmation.
A state can be arranged/reorganized, alongside people setting up their household; same ordering/setting-up meaning.
Organising an event and arranging a territory support round-one institutional extension of arranging a state, without a separate political or conspiratorial sense.
